data.written: 2026-10-13, pin 4 v6 (backlog 4, the yardstick redo): by eye from the pin (Pinterest pin 783485666539777050, motorcycle-outfit-men board, number 4, 'mirror camera selfie shirtless', 960x1200) with a brightened, gridded copy, and from the 2026-10-01 inventories v1-v5 (FEEDBACK_LEDGER: 14 pictures, 1 passed, Pro with the measured FRAMING line; the Flash misses were all the pose gate: size in the frame shoulders-to-nose x1.08-1.25, shoulder midpoint 0.047-0.087 off, head 0.046-0.054 off), whose kept parts are carried over: the very close crop, the blurred raised hand, the camera, the strap, the dark band, the panel, the grey wall. What is new is by the user's yardstick of 2026-10-10 ('any shirtless picture will get the fully pumped version of mine'): the recipe takes --physique pumped-front-torso (pumped_front.jpg cut at the chin and the waistband, so the standard's hanging arms cannot set his pose; this pin's arms are raised and bent, FAILURE_LOG F19/F22, and pin 8 v7 held its pose gate on its second picture with the same standard), his janeu and his silver neck chain on the bare chest (checklist item 36), character me@v2 (the lean face and the current cut), no jewellery or tattoo that is not his (the pin shows none; the brown leather loop on the picture-right wrist is the camera strap's). The v5 text said the camera is held 'with both hands': wrong, one hand (the picture-right hand) grips it from above, the other arm is raised on the wall; v6 says so. THE MIRROR: this pin is a true, unflipped reflection. Proof: the small FUJIFILM lettering on the camera's front plate reads backwards in the pin (mirror writing; checked on an 8x crop against the 2026-10-01 picture, where Gemini wrote it the normal way round, a mismatch with item 34), the camera is held in the hand at picture-right (the right-handed man's usual way round) and the raised hand on the wall is at picture-left. So his LEFT side is at picture-LEFT and his RIGHT side at picture-RIGHT, as on pin 8 (FEEDBACK of pin 8 v7: 'his LEFT shoulder is at picture-LEFT'). In his own front photos his left shoulder is at picture-right (BODY reference: the thread falls from picture-right); a mirror flips it, so here his janeu comes over the top of the picture-LEFT shoulder beside the neck. The pin 8 picture of this redo (run 20261013_190541) drew the thread as a cord from the phone hand, i.e. it followed the BODY reference's side instead of the words, so this janeu item states the side three times and forbids the other side and any thread from a hand, the camera or the strap. Geometry read off the pin (960x1200): picture-left shoulder top beside the neck base at about (280-300, 800-830), the neck base between x 300 and 500 at y 850, the sternum groove at about x 390 for y 1100-1200, his chest between the raised arm's inner edge (x 200) and the torso's right edge (x 510) at the bottom, the camera at x 390-530 and y 555-750 (lens centre about 460, 655), the strap's lug at about (430, 775) and its U across the upper chest to the picture-right arm below the elbow, buckle at about (768, 725). In his BODY reference the thread hangs nearly straight down, slanting only about 12 degrees toward his right hip (FAILURE_LOG F24: judged beside his photo), and in this frame only the upper chest shows (neck base to the bottom edge, about 350 px), so the visible thread is a near-vertical line of about 350 px that moves only about 75 px toward the middle. Sizes: the raised upper arm is at least 165 px wide beside a head about 230 px wide (0.7 head widths, cut by the left edge), his upper arm in the BODY reference is about 0.47 head widths, so his arms are about a third thinner; written conservatively as 'about a quarter' (pin 15 withdrew 'a third thinner'); his shoulders are written 'about a fifth narrower' as on pin 8. The old runs (FAILURE_LOG P4) show the body following the pin man's, so the shoulder and arm items name the size difference, and the paste mask (the pin man's outline grown) holds his narrower build while the restore fills the freed wall from Gemini's own wall. Keep lines name the people (none but him, item 33) and the lettering (the camera's own, kept as it is, item 34). A free restore test of the old v3 on this pin (tools/background_restore.py --goal ... --sample the old v1_0.jpg; 52 percent of the frame copied from the pin, ECC fit fine) showed pale halos on the wall where the pin man's wide arm and shoulder had been, because the freed wall comes from Gemini's own wall inside the paste mask; the 'wall his narrower build frees' item asks for plain wall there with no outline of the old arms. The shoulder line keeps the pin's height (70 percent) because the pose gate's shoulders-to-nose size failed at x1.08-1.25 in 8 of 12 old Flash pictures and a flatter trapezius could lower it.
